statement: Define S to be the set of cells (i,j) with 0 <= i < m, 0 <= j < n, low <= grid[i][j] <= high, that are reachable from (sr,sc) by a path of adjacent cells all having grid > 0. For (i,j) in S let d(i,j) be the length (number of steps) of a shortest such path. For distinct a=(r1,c1) and b=(r2,c2) in S, write rank_better(a,b) iff the tuple (d(a), grid[r1][c1], r1, c1) is lexicographically smaller than the tuple (d(b), grid[r2][c2], r2, c2). The function returns a result r such that: (1) len(r) = min(k, |S|); (2) for every t with 0 <= t < len(r), r[t] is a vector of length 2 and cell(r[t]) = (r[t][0], r[t][1]) belongs to S; (3) the cells cell(r[0]), ..., cell(r[len(r)-1]) are pairwise distinct; (4) for every t with 0 <= t < len(r)-1, rank_better(cell(r[t]), cell(r[t+1])); (5) for every cell x in S that is not equal to any cell(r[t]) with 0 <= t < len(r), and for every t with 0 <= t < len(r), rank_better(cell(r[t]), x).
preconditions: m = len(grid) >= 1; there exists n >= 1 such that every row grid[i] (0 <= i < m) has length n and 1 <= m*n <= 100000; every grid[i][j] satisfies 0 <= grid[i][j] <= 100000; len(pricing) = 2, low = pricing[0], high = pricing[1], and 2 <= low <= high <= 100000; len(start) = 2, sr = start[0], sc = start[1], with 0 <= sr < m, 0 <= sc < n, and grid[sr][sc] > 0; 1 <= k <= m*n.
